macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks fall sharply ahead of Nvidia results
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.64% to 50,759.42, the S&P 500 dropped 1.03% to 7,340.53, and the Nasdaq Composite declined 0.74% to 24,328.38. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq recorded four consecutive losing sessions as technology stocks remained under pressure.

items.title: Nvidia beats estimates and issues strong outlook
items.summary: Nvidia reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of about $115.8 billion, up 103% year over year, with data-center revenue of $107.6 billion. Its roughly $130 billion fourth-quarter revenue forecast exceeded expectations, sending shares up as much as 4.8% after hours and easing concerns about AI demand.

items.title: U.S. stock futures rebound on Nvidia optimism
items.summary: S&P 500 futures rose about 0.6%, Nasdaq-100 futures gained roughly 0.6% to 1%, and Dow futures added about 0.2% after Nvidia’s results. The rebound followed the previous session’s broad selloff and was concentrated in semiconductor and other technology shares.

items.title: Fed officials signal openness to larger rate hike
items.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank may need to consider a 50-basis-point increase to bring persistent inflation under control. Markets were pricing a near-certain 25-basis-point hike at the December meeting, while investors awaited minutes from the Fed’s October meeting.

items.title: Fed minutes become the next major market catalyst
items.summary: The Federal Reserve was scheduled to release minutes from its October meeting, when policymakers held the federal funds target range at 3.75% to 4%. Investors are looking for evidence of how concerned officials are about persistent inflation and whether further tightening is likely.

items.title: European markets stabilize after Nvidia earnings
items.summary: The pan-European STOXX 600 was broadly steady after falling 1.75% in the prior session, its steepest one-day decline since March. Nvidia’s results lifted European semiconductor shares, while investors also awaited euro-area inflation data and the Fed minutes.

items.title: Asian equities mixed as Nvidia offsets Wall Street losses
items.summary: South Korea’s KOSPI rose 1.4% and Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained 0.4% as Nvidia’s positive outlook supported technology stocks. The gains followed declines of 1.6% for the Dow, 1% for the S&P 500, and 0.7% for the Nasdaq Composite in the previous U.S. session.

items.title: U.K. inflation rises to one-year high
items.summary: Annual U.K. inflation increased to 3.6% in October from 3.5% in September, adding to concerns about persistent price pressures. The data contributed to caution around the outlook for central-bank policy and bond yields.

items.title: Treasury yields remain elevated amid hawkish Fed expectations
items.summary: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield was around 5.10% during European trading after a strong multi-week rise. Resilient U.S. retail sales and expectations for additional Fed tightening continued to support higher yields and a stronger dollar.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin trades near $64,310 as market liquidity weakens
items.summary: Bitcoin was reported near $64,310, with its recovery toward $64,000–$65,000 facing pressure from contracting stablecoin liquidity. Glassnode identified $62,000–$66,000 as a key support zone, with a break below $62,000 potentially exposing lower levels.

items.title: North Korea-linked wallet moves $137 million in Ether
items.summary: A wallet linked to the October Binance attack moved about 74,881 ETH, valued near $137 million, across multiple addresses. The FBI attributed the attack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, while authorities have pursued seizure or freezing of related assets.

items.title: Ethereum developers consider sharply higher gas limit
items.summary: Ethereum proposals EIP-8037 and EIP-8038 would raise the per-block gas limit from 60 million to as much as 200 million. Developers are still evaluating the change after an audit identified roughly 200 affected contract types.

items.title: Strategy buys 485 Bitcoin for $33.4 million
items.summary: Strategy purchased 485 BTC for approximately $33.4 million while also spending about $228.1 million on repurchasing STRC preferred shares, largely funded through sales of common stock.

items.title: U.S. senators question SEC tokenization exemption
items.summary: Four Democratic senators questioned the SEC’s five-year innovation exemption for tokenized securities, raising concerns that the framework could create anti-money-laundering and investor-protection gaps.

items.title: Coinbase expands crypto-collateralized USDC borrowing
items.summary: Coinbase opened borrowing services backed by BTC, ETH and SOL collateral across all 50 U.S. states. The platform also reported blocking $4.7 million linked to a fraudulent livestream impersonating Elon Musk.

items.title: Acala votes to shut down network
items.summary: Acala approved a plan to shut down its network and stop producing blocks on February 10, 2027.

items.title: Russia adds Alfa-Bank to digital-currency exchange registry
items.summary: Russia’s central bank reportedly added Alfa-Bank to its registry of institutions authorized to operate digital-currency exchange services.

items.title: Codex raises $30 million for stablecoin payments
items.summary: Stablecoin payments company Codex completed a $30 million Series A funding round led by Pantera Capital.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra for demanding tasks and GPT-6.2 Sol as a lower-cost model for everyday coding and writing across ChatGPT Work, Codex, and its API on November 17.[1]

items.title: Nvidia unveils GR00T 2 robotics model
items.summary: Nvidia introduced GR00T 2, an open robotics world-action model designed to learn from human video and predict how robot actions will change its surroundings.[1]

items.title: Tencent open-sources Hunyuan Hy4 Flash
items.summary: Tencent released Hy4 Flash in multiple variants, describing it as a multimodal model with 224 billion total parameters, 12 billion active parameters per token, and support for contexts up to one million tokens.[1]

items.title: Microsoft expands its in-house MAI model lineup
items.summary: Microsoft announced new MAI capabilities spanning coding, image generation, voice, transcription, cybersecurity, and decision models at Ignite 2026, with deployment through Microsoft Foundry, Copilot, and security products.[1]

items.title: Baseten models enter Microsoft Foundry preview
items.summary: Baseten models including DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM-5.3, GLM-5.3-Flash, and Kimi K3 became available in public preview for Azure customers through Microsoft Foundry.[1]

items.title: ElevenLabs to acquire Japanese voice-AI lab Kotoba
items.summary: ElevenLabs announced plans to acquire Kotoba, a Japanese voice-AI company developing speech generation, transcription, and simultaneous-interpretation technology; the deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026.[1]

items.title: Xpeng’s Turing AI chip nears mass production
items.summary: Xpeng’s Turing chip, designed for full-stack vehicle autonomy, reportedly reaches 700 TOPS and is expected to debut in an upcoming Xpeng vehicle as the company challenges Nvidia in automotive AI hardware.[1]

items.title: Luminary introduces autonomous physics-AI workflow
items.summary: Luminary launched Autopilot, which automates physics-AI tasks such as CAD ingestion, meshing, data generation, training, and inference; the company also introduced continually improving large physics models.[1]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches amid enormous hype
items.summary: Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled to launch Thursday, returning players to Vice City after a 13-year gap since Grand Theft Auto V. The release is expected to become a major cultural and commercial event.

items.title: Esports Awards 2026 announce winners
items.summary: OpTic Texas won Esports Team of the Year, Team Vitality took Esports Organization of the Year, and Counter-Strike 2 was named Esports Game of the Year. Mobile Legends: Bang Bang won Esports Mobile Game of the Year.

items.title: Firaxis reportedly cuts about 60 jobs
items.summary: Firaxis Games, the developer behind Civilization and XCOM, is reportedly cutting approximately 60 positions, said to represent about one-third of its workforce.

items.title: 9 Kings leaves Early Access
items.summary: Sad Socket and Hooded Horse’s strategy game 9 Kings has officially exited Early Access after more than 18 months of development.

items.title: Xsolla expands developer platform with Quest Builder and Backpack
items.summary: Xsolla introduced Quest Builder and Backpack, tools intended to help developers and brands use digital items to attract and retain players.

items.title: North-west German esports associations form regional federation
items.summary: Esports associations in Bremen, Hamburg and Lower Saxony are merging to create the E-Sport-Verband Nordwest, a new regional organization for Germany’s organized esports scene.
